title: 2019 AMC 12A Problem 11
statement: For some positive integer \(k,\) the repeating base-\(k\) representation of the (base-ten) fraction \(\dfrac{7}{51}\) is \(0.\overline{23}_k = 0.232323\ldots_k.\) What is \(k?\)

solutions.text:
The repeating block gives \[ 0.\overline{23}_k = \dfrac{2k + 3}{k^2 - 1} = \dfrac{7}{51}. \]

Cross-multiplying, \(51(2k + 3) = 7(k^2 - 1),\) so \(7k^2 - 102k - 160 = 0.\)

The quadratic formula gives \[ \begin{aligned} k &= \dfrac{102 + \sqrt{14884}}{14} \\ &= \dfrac{102 + 122}{14} = 16. \end{aligned} \]

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: A two-digit repeating block in base \(k\) equals \(\dfrac{2k + 3}{k^2 - 1}\)
